products.title: Control to Pass Gi Pressure Passing by Diego Pato
products.body:
Pressure passing is the most reliable way to break a guard player in the gi, and few people have proven it at a higher level than Diego Pato.

  • A five-time IBJJF World Champion, two-time IBJJF No-Gi World Champion and Pan Champion, Diego Pato is one of the most decorated light featherweights the sport has ever produced
  • In Control To Pass, Pato teaches the pressure passing system he built on the Grand Slam circuit, from the first approach and the fight for the hips all the way to the pass.
  • This isn't a random collection of passes, it's the answer to the guards that actually show up in competition: De La Riva, reverse De La Riva, and anyone who frames to keep you at range.

What Will You Learn?

Pressure passing is the most reliable way to break a guard player in the gi, and few people have proven it at a higher level than Diego Pato.

A five-time IBJJF World Champion, two-time IBJJF No-Gi World Champion and Pan Champion, Diego Pato is one of the most decorated light featherweights the sport has ever produced. Now he is sharing the passing system he used to get there, the same one he says he has been building through his competition run on the Grand Slams.

In Control To Pass, Pato breaks down how to approach the guard, crowd the hips, hold your base while your opponent frames, and create the reaction that gives you the pass. This isn't a random collection of passes, it's a step by step method for making your opponent carry your weight until the guard falls apart.

The course is built around the guards you actually run into. Pato shows you how to escape De La Riva straight into a pressure pass, how to deal with reverse De La Riva by going to the knee cut, and how his crazy dog pass forces the reaction that opens everything else. Every position starts from the same idea: take the space away first, then pass.

Unlike passes that only work on a tired or flat opponent, pressure travels. Once you understand how to crowd the hips and stay heavy while your opponent moves, the knee slice, the leg smash and the double armpit stop being separate techniques and start being different finishes to the same problem.

If you have ever felt your passing work in the first round and disappear by the third, the answer is usually not a new technique. It is where your weight is before the technique even starts.

Learn how one of the most decorated light featherweights in the world turns simple pressure into a complete gi passing system.

What Exactly Do You Get?

Part 1: Building the Pressure Passing Foundation

  • Side to Side Approach Drill
  • Crowding the Hips
  • Maintain Base and Dealing with Frames
  • Crazy Dog to Create Reaction
  • Live Action Drills

Part 2: Passing Attacks and Beating the Open Guard

  • Knee Slice to Create Reaction
  • Leg Smash
  • Live Action Drill
  • Base Against De La Riva and Inside Pressure Passing
  • Double Armpit

products.title: The Pressure Passing Manual by Marco Barbosa
products.body:
Learn the Jaw Breaking, Ear Bursting Pressure Passing Secrets From Murilo Sanatana’s Coach Marco Barbosa “The God Father Of Pressure”.. This 53 Year Old Probably Generates More Top Pressure Than Anyone Else In The World

  • Learn The Skill Of Applying “Make Them Quit” Pressure From One Of The Black Belt OG’s of Sao Paulo
  • Off the mats, pressure can turn coal into diamonds. On the mat, pressure can turn you into a completely new fighter.
  • Marco draws back the curtain and lets you in on all of his secrets
  • These are moves that will work for you, no matter who you are facing. Look no further than Marco's Pressure Passing Manual
  • Change your game

Check Out The Trailer!

What Will You Learn?

Off the mats, pressure can turn coal into diamonds. On the mat, pressure can turn you into a completely new fighter.

Being able to use your leverage and weight in the right ways to create all of the organ-squishing pressure that you want is NOT about being big and strong, it’s a skill that you can perfect over time! We all spend a lot of time on the mats, pretty much every warm-up, hip escaping and shrimping and learning how to create space. Now, it’s time to flip that on its head and study how to *take that space away* and replace it with the pressure you need to change the fight.

For this important skill, we are partnering with one of the most respected pressure passing coaches in the world Marco Barbosa, “The Godfather of Pressure”, to show you all of the old school ways he uses to control people half his age and twice his size. A black belt in judo and Brazilian jiu-jitsu, Marco has spent his life studying the gentle art and finding ways to add his own savage style to it. He’s developed a top game that feeds off of the pressure he creates, and when he gets on top it is like trying to move a truck.



If you want to pass a guard, it isn’t as simple as just doing a knee slide or an over-under pass. You must build the position on proper fundamentals! Not only will this instructional series give you the ways to pass, it will show you just how to deconstruct the guard and build a passing game that gives you every advantage possible, no matter your body type.

More than just working on himself, Marco is one of the best coaches in the world! You are getting premium technique from one of the best instructors of his generation, on this multi-volume set, which makes this a can’t miss! See the pressure system that fighters like Murilo Santana and the Miyao brothers have been using at the highest levels, and get the same instruction on how to make pressure a regular part of your game.

New school jiu-jitsu may favor what’s new and most impressive-looking, but those old-school grapplers down in Brazil cared about one thing: effectiveness. Maybe it isn’t flashy, but it works, and it works in gi, no gi, or off the mat if you need it. Come get that old school feel and understand how a traditional black belt from a different generation still blows through the guard like a much younger man.

See How This 53-Year Old Puts The Hurt On Guys Half His Age And Twice His Size!

This two-volume instructional set doesn’t just launch into techniques, Marco steps back to really explain what the little invisible battles between top and bottom are, and how to win them after you really recognize them. Build your skillset with drill after drill that will teach you the pressuring instincts you need, perfect for warming up with every time you hit the mat. This also really gives time for Marco to explain those finer points that he has mastered with a lifetime of experience. Once your fundamentals are on point, you can start to use them to smash, crash, and pass from position to position.



Pressure passing isn’t just stacking and squeezing, it’s a way of life. See how to apply your body and leverage in the right ways so that no matter what, you can keep your partners and opponents pinned down while you work. If people are wriggling free from you, even after you have passed their guard, then you need to see the carefully applied controls that Marco uses to stabilize himself before progressing along to the next position, or finishing with the submission.

So, What's On The Series?

Part 2

products.title: No-Gi Ankle Locks To Heel Hooks by Diego Pato
products.body:
Most grapplers treat the straight ankle lock as the submission they settle for, and Diego Pato turned it into the doorway to the heel hook.

  • A five-time IBJJF World Champion, two-time IBJJF No-Gi World Champion, Pan Champion and two-time ADCC medalist, Diego Pato is one of the most decorated light featherweights the sport has ever produced
  • In No-Gi Ankle Locks To Heel Hooks, Pato shows how he enters the position, keeps his grip while the opponent defends, and converts a straight ankle lock into a heel hook finish.
  • This isn't a leg lock highlight reel, it's one connected path from the entry to the finish, built on the concepts he says have carried him through training and competition.

What Will You Learn?

Most grapplers treat the straight ankle lock as the submission they settle for, and Diego Pato turned it into the doorway to the heel hook.

A five-time IBJJF World Champion, two-time IBJJF No-Gi World Champion, Pan Champion and two-time ADCC medalist, Diego Pato is one of the most decorated light featherweights the sport has ever produced, and the straight ankle lock is one of the two submissions he is best known for. Here he steps out of the gi to teach the leg lock concepts he uses in training and competition.

In No-Gi Ankle Locks To Heel Hooks, Pato starts with what a finishing ankle lock actually requires, then shows how to enter the position, how to pass and keep the grip while your opponent fights it, and how that same grip walks you into the heel hook. This isn't a leg lock highlight reel, it's one connected path from the entry to the finish.

The course also carries his own stamp. The Pato Lock and the Kiss of the Tilapia finish sit right next to the Kiss of the Dragon entry, along with how to break the posture of an opponent who is defending well and how to apply the same mechanics from everywhere else.

Leg locks fail for most people at the same place: the grip dies the moment the opponent starts to move. Pato's answer is not a stronger squeeze, it is understanding what the grip is doing and where the finish is hiding when the ankle lock alone is not enough.

If your leg attacks stall out against anyone who knows how to defend, the problem is usually the connection between positions, not the submission itself.

Learn how one of the most decorated light featherweights in the world builds a finishing leg lock game from the ankle up.

What Exactly Do You Get?

Part 1: Entering and Building the Ankle Lock

  • Ankle Lock Finish Overview
  • Enter the Position
  • Passing and Maintain the Grip
  • Kiss of the Dragon Entry
  • Ankle Lock Grip Leads to Heel Hook

Part 2: Finishes and Applying the System

  • Pato Lock
  • Kiss of the Tilapia Finish
  • Breaking the Posture
  • Applying It Everywhere
